lines: Picture a bank's platform team with a promising prototype assistant.
Under the hood, it's glued together from whatever libraries were handy.
First, customer data can never leave the bank's own infrastructure.
So the model runs on a home-made server that crawls under real traffic.
Second, there are no guardrails.
A tester talks the assistant into ignoring its rules, and nothing stops it.
Third, there's no evaluation gate.
When a fine-tuned model arrives, nobody can say if it beats the old one.
So the team stops adding libraries.
Instead, they map each need to one component with exactly one job.
For serving, they pick NIM: a prebuilt, GPU-optimised model container running in their own data centre.
Its OpenAI-compatible API means the agent code barely changes.

say.1: Its open A-I compatible A-P-I means the agent code barely changes.
